bihar_raw_news.title: Gaya-Bangkok Flight Launch Opens New Route for Bihar Tourism - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Gaya-Bangkok Flight Launch Opens New Route for Bihar Tourism Breaking News Gaya-Bangkok Flight Launch Opens New Route for Bihar Tourism By Maria Dsouza October 27, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Monday flagged off IndiGo’s first non-stop flight from Gaya to Bangkok, adding a twice-weekly international service aimed at improving access to Bodh Gaya and strengthening air links between Bihar and Thailand. The flight was inaugurated through videoconferencing at a ceremony in Patna. Choudhary greeted passengers on the inaugural service and said the new connection would strengthen religious, cultural and tourism ties between Bihar and Thailand. Gaya is the principal air gateway to Bodh Gaya, one of the world’s most important Buddhist pilgrimage destinations. The chief minister said the direct service would make travel easier for international visitors and support tourism across the Magadh region. The route is being launched ahead of the pilgrim season, when Gaya Airport is preparing for an increase in domestic and foreign tourist movement under its winter schedule. The new service is expected to support hotels, transport operators, handicraft businesses and other enterprises dependent on tourism. Choudhary said improved air connectivity would help Bihar give wider international recognition to its cultural heritage, historical sites and local products. The launch is part of a broader state effort to expand aviation access through airports in Patna, Darbhanga, Gaya and Purnia. Choudhary said the state was working on a policy to increase connectivity on new international routes, with expected support from IndiGo. He also said coordination to expand international air services in Bihar would continue. Gaya’s international network has expanded in recent days. Thailand-based Thai Airways began direct flights to Bangkok over the weekend, while Thai AirAsia started a service connecting Gaya with Don Mueang. Thai AirAsia’s flights are scheduled to operate three days a week—Tuesday, Friday and Sunday—until March 26, 2027. Domestic connectivity has also increased. Air India began two services on the Delhi-Gaya-Delhi route from Sunday, with the airline’s winter schedule scheduled to remain in operation until March 27, 2027. The expansion gives pilgrims and tourists more direct travel options during the period of higher seasonal demand. It also places additional importance on the ability of Gaya Airport and local tourism-linked services to manage international arrivals, onward transport and visitor requirements. The state government’s proposed international connectivity policy is expected to guide further route expansion. national_raw_news.title: Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan reviews preparedness for Cyclone Arnab in Bay of Bengal
national_raw_news.content: Cabinet Secretary, Dr. T. V. Somanathan today chaired a meeting of the National Crisis Management Committee to review preparedness for the impending cyclone in the Bay of Bengal. During the meeting, it was informed that adequate shelters and evacuation arrangements have been made, and necessary NDRF and SDRF teams have been kept on standby. District Control Rooms have also been activated and they are monitoring the situation. On the occasion, Dr Somanathan said that essential services should be restored in the shortest possible time in the event of any damage. He also stressed that the objective should be to ensure zero loss of life and minimise damage to property and infrastructure. He also directed Ministry of Home Affairs and India Meteorological Department (IMD) to alert Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar incase of heavy rainfall in the area. Director General, IMD, Dr. Mrutyunjay Mohapatra briefed the Committee that the deep depression over East central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal has moved nearly Westwards and intensified into cyclonic storm ARNAB. It is likely to affect districts in Telangana, Southern Odisha, South and Central Chhattisgarh apart from Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. The Chief Secretaries and senior officials of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Puducherry apprised the Committee of the preparatory measures being undertaken by the State Governments and local administration. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the Southwest and adjoining central Bay of Bengal, and along and off the coasts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Yanam (Puducherry) till Thursday.

national_raw_news.content: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has cleared various capital acquisition proposals of the Defence Forces at an estimated cost of around 2 lakh and 12 thousand crore rupees. Ministry of Defence has said that nearly 82% of the procurements will be made from Indian Industry. For the Indian Army, approval was accorded for the procurement of various system including High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System, Light Multi Role Helicopters (LMRH), Very Short-Range Air Defence System, Surveillance UAV, Integrated Surveillance and Strike System and Long Range Kamikaze Drone System. The High Mobility Vehicles which will be procured for India Army will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System will provide matching mobility and firepower to mechanised formations. The Light Multi Role Helicopters will be used by both the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force for Surveillance, Combat, Search and Rescue of troops, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief, among others. The surveillance and Drone Systems will enhance the surveillance and targeting capabilities of the Indian Army. For the Indian Navy, approval was given for the procurement of Active Offboard Decoy System and other major Naval platforms. This will enhance the credibility of anti-missiles defence, especially against modern anti-ship missiles of adversaries. For the Indian Air Force, approval was accorded for the procurement of Helicopters, Air Defence Systems, Weapons and Mobile X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System to enhance the air defence and warfighting capabilities. The procurement of Special Utility Helicopters will help the Indian Air Force to meet the important air transport requirements. The X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System will provide high-resolution, localised weather surveillance in forward areas.

national_raw_news.title: Commerce Ministry extends RELIEF scheme for exporters until March 31, 2027
national_raw_news.content: The Department of Commerce has extended the timelines under Component II of Resilience and Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation (RELIEF) until the 31st March of next year. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the extension has been notified in view of continued geopolitical disruptions in West Asia and their impact on maritime logistics across the Gulf and adjoining regions. RELIEF is a time-bound intervention under the Export Promotion Mission. Component II of the initiative aims to encourage exporters to obtain Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India cover for upcoming shipments to specified regions by providing 95 per cent risk coverage. The benefit is available for Standalone Policies and Whole Turnover Policies obtained on or after 16th of this year. Under this component, the premium payable by eligible exporters is protected against increases beyond pre-disruption levels during the eligible period. The covered cargo categories include Full Container Load, Less than Container Load and refrigerated containers, excluding energy shipments. Exporters seeking coverage under the RELIEF initiative are required to submit claims and supporting documents through the ECGC customer portal at www.ecgcltd.in. RELIEF launched on 19th of March this year, is a targeted intervention to support Indian exporters facing extraordinary freight cost escalation, higher insurance premia and war-related export risks arising from disruptions in the Gulf and the wider West Asian maritime corridor.

national_raw_news.title: ECI suspends six officials, including four policemen, over alleged lapses at few polling stations of Agra 2 hours ago 14
national_raw_news.content: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has issued orders for placing six officials, including four policemen, under suspension for alleged lapses at a few polling stations of Agra Division Teachers’ Constituency on 23rd of this month. According to an ECI statement, the suspensions were ordered on the basis of an inquiry report filed by the Divisional Commissioner, Agra-cum-Returning Officer for Agra Division Teachers’ Constituency. The ECI said in a letter issued to the Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh that the six delinquent officials would face charge sheets and another 21 polling officials shall face disciplinary proceedings. The ECI observed that the officers entrusted with supervisory responsibilities failed to ensure effective supervision and maintain proper control within and in the vicinity of the polling stations. It said, such dereliction of duty on the part of officers holding supervisory positions is viewed seriously and cannot be condoned. Meanwhile, a re-poll was held today at polling stations number 20, 21 and 26 of Agra Division Teachers’ Constituency for the biennial election to the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council. Polling in 11 MLC constituencies (five graduate and six teachers’ constituencies of the Legislative Council) was held on Friday. A total of 152 candidates were in the fray.

national_raw_news.content: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has said that parliaments can play an important role in strengthening mutual understanding and trust, reducing international tensions and finding peaceful solutions to global challenges. Addressing the inaugural session of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in New Delhi, Mr Birla highlighted challenges such as regional conflicts, wars, economic instability, trade tensions, terrorism and climate change. He stressed the need for solutions that improve citizens’ lives and contribute to a more inclusive and peaceful world. Mr Birla expressed confidence that the deliberations at this forum will give a new direction to the mutual trust and cooperation and further strengthen the shared commitment to people-centric development. He said, together, this forum will build a parliamentary partnership that creates new opportunities for peace, prosperity, and sustainable development and contributes to fulfilling the aspirations of the people. The Speaker added that BRICS aspires to strengthen the voice of the Global South. Mr Birla said that the unanimous adoption of the Joint declaration at the BRICS Summit held in New Delhi under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is a major achievement. Mr Birla underlined that the aspirations of BRICS countries must not remain confined to deliberations but must translate into concrete policies and practical cooperation. Lok Sabha Speaker Birla underlined that the parliaments have a responsibility to understand the aspirations of young people, provide space for their voices, and connect their talents with nation-building. He said, the true strength of parliamentary diplomacy lies in incorporating a democratic perspective into international relations while respecting one another’s sovereignty. Describing India as the mother of democracy, Mr Birla highlighted that India’s democratic strength lies in dialogue, diversity of opinions and mutual respect. He noted that through this democratic foundation, India is steadily advancing on its development journey. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also attended the inaugural session of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum at the Central Hall, Samvidhan Sadan, Parliament House. Mr Modi also met the leaders of the visiting delegations. Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh described India as a repository of knowledge, wisdom and civilizational heritage, reflecting its rich diversity of cultures, languages and traditions. Mr. Harivansh said BRICS, representing nearly half of the world’s population, has emerged as an effective multilateral platform for consultation and cooperation on issues of global and regional significance. He said that under India’s BRICS Presidency in New Delhi this year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has advanced a transformative vision centred on people and humanity. He also highlighted India’s efforts to strengthen the voice of the Global South and promote reforms in global governance, contributing towards a more balanced multipolar world order. Referring to the theme of the inaugural session, Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development, Harivansh said parliaments must remain vigilant, responsive, dynamic and future-ready to address emerging challenges, including economic uncertainties, technological transformation, climate change, public health emergencies and social inequalities. He expressed confidence that the deliberations would enable delegates to exchange experiences, learn from one another and identify parliamentary approaches to improve the lives of people. Earlier, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla welcomed the leaders of the parliamentary delegation of eleven BRICS Member countries and 10 Partner countries. The two-day event will conclude tomorrow.

national_raw_news.title: Brazil’s left-wing President Lula da Silva elected for fourth term
national_raw_news.content: In Brazil, Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil’s intense presidential race. With this victory, Lula has become the only politician in modern Brazilian history who successfully rebound and win the second round after falling behind in the first. Incumbent Lula won the final runoff election with 51 percent of the vote and more than 51.49 million ballots. Meanwhile, Bolsonaro received 48.68 percent of the vote, which amounted to 48.8 million ballots. Just over 2.6 million votes separated the two candidates. Because of the close and highly contested race, voting stations across the country remained open two hours longer than originally planned. The former metalworker union leader, at the age of 80 will be sworn into office on 5th of January next year, breaking his own record as the oldest president to take the oath of office since Brazil returned to a democracy. This victory marks an unprecedented fourth non-consecutive term for Lula, who has run for the presidency a total of seven times. During his campaign, Lula has rallied supporters around cost-of-living issues. He championed a constitutional amendment passed this month that reduces the Brazilian workweek, and floated the possibility of providing free public transport on weekends. Lula’s victory stops a recent regional trend in South America, where right-wing leaders have swept recent presidential elections in nearby countries like Peru, Colombia, Argentina, Bolivia, and Ecuador.

national_raw_news.title: India to expand its space operations with four functional launch pads by 2029, says ISRO Chairman
national_raw_news.content: ISRO Chairman V Narayanan has said that India will expand its space operations significantly with four functional launch pads by the year 2029. Mr. Narayanan said, these include a 2000 acre dedicated Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) complex at Kulasekarapattinam in Tuticorin district of Tamil Nadu and a third launch pad at Sriharikota, to meet the global demand for satellite launches. He was addressing convocation of a private university at Porur near Chennai. The ISRO chief said that the upcoming Kulasekarapattinam spaceport facility will feature crucial infrastructure such as integration buildings, launch pads, rail-track systems, telemetry, tracking, and command systems. Mr. Narayanan stated that ISRO plans to conduct the first uncrewed Gaganyaan test within the next two months, followed by two subsequent uncrewed tests before the crewed mission. These preliminary tests will evaluate environmental control, safety systems, crew escape mechanisms, and module interiors under varying pressure, temperature, and humidity conditions. ISRO successfully conducted approximately 8 thousand ground-based experiments for the mission, and four astronaut-designates are currently undergoing specialised training. Mr. Narayanan further revealed plans for Chandrayaan-5, a collaborative lunar mission with Japan’s space agency featuring a 350 kg rover designed to conduct 100 days of surface experiments. He also clarified that the national space agency will not be privatised. ISRO Chairman emphasised that partnering with private firms was essential to meet surging global and domestic demands for thousands of satellites.

national_raw_news.content: The Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South Odisha coasts have been placed under an Orange Alert as a Deep Depression over the East Central and Southeast Bay of Bengal rapidly intensifies into a major storm system. To counter the threat, the Andhra Pradesh state government is actively coordinating across all departments to deploy emergency resources, secure vulnerable areas, and prevent loss of life and property. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the system is moving west-northwestward at 15 kmph and was last located roughly 730 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 990 km east of Bapatla. It was strengthened into a cyclonic storm during early hours, escalate into a severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow, and peak as a very severe cyclonic storm as it nears the West Central Bay of Bengal. Landfall is expected by the forenoon of October 28, crossing the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam with destructive sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, gusting up to 140 kmph. In anticipation of the cyclone’s impact, the IMD has warned of widespread heavy rainfall over the next two days and has urged the public to remain on high alert. Residents are strongly advised to postpone any travel plans, while fishermen have been strictly ordered not to venture into the sea.

national_raw_news.title: Use of terrorism as instrument of statecraft cannot be justified or rationalised, says EAM S Jais...
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has said that the use of terrorism as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable, and it can never be justified or rationalised. He said, terrorism continues because not all states display zero tolerance for the menace. Dr Jaishankar was addressing an event held in New Delhi to mark 75th anniversary of Chinmaya Mission. He said, the world must develop sharper awareness about this common threat, and it must come together with stronger resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. He underlined the importance of peace, especially amid the ongoing conflicts in the world, and cautioned that war anywhere threatens peace everywhere. Dr Jaishankar cited the two major conflicts going on in the world, in Ukraine and in West Asia, and said societies and economies and people far away who have little say in the matter are actually paying the cost. External Affairs Minister said, India expresses global sentiment when we urge that dialogue and diplomacy are the only solution. The minister underlined that India is making efforts towards peace building and is open to working with other partners to that end. Dr Jaishankar reiterated that the Global South today faces a ‘4F’ crisis — of finance, fuel, food and fertiliser and said the Global North must realise that it has “equal stakes” in finding solutions. He said, international economy must be urgently derisked and nations provided with more diversified options. Stressing the need for a genuine dialogue, the minister said, market distortions through constriction and chokepoints only add to suffering. Dr Jaishankar said, United Nations must show leadership, and not be a spectator to global crises. He asserted that the case for reformed multilateralism gets stronger by the day.

national_raw_news.title: Deep depression over Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into cyclonic storm today 2 hours ago 136
national_raw_news.content: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the Deep Depression over Bay of Bengal will intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm today. IMD has advised the fisherman not to venture into West central and adjoining Northwest and Southwest Bay of Bengal during the next two days. Talking to Akashvani News, Director General of IMD, Dr Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said, due to influence of depression the sea condition is very rough and will deteriorate further. He said that the wind speed may lead to large scale damage of structures and standing crops. He said that heavy to extremely heavy rainfall may hit parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh during the next two days. Dr Mohapatra added that due to heavy rainfall can cause flooding in low-lying areas and landslides in hilly areas and urged the people living in these regions to be cautious. Meanwhile, the Weather Agency has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for today. Heavy Rainfall is also expected over Coastal Andhra Pradesh till tomorrow. Met Department has predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Gangetic West Bengal, Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two days.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi Inaugurates RBI’s Data Centre, Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, describing the facilities as an important step towards strengthening India’s digital infrastructure and safeguarding its financial system against emerging cyber threats. Invoking the blessings of Lord Jagannath, PM Modi said the inauguration marked a significant occasion for Odisha and the country. He congratulated the RBI and all those associated with establishing the two facilities. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister said India’s governance model was driven by the principles of pro-people, proactive and good governance, with a focus on equitable development and ensuring that opportunities reach villages and smaller towns. He highlighted the expansion of infrastructure, healthcare facilities and digital connectivity, saying that improving citizens’ lives and creating new opportunities had become central to governance. Digital Banking Expands Financial Inclusion PM Modi said India had witnessed a major transformation in financial inclusion, with digital banking connecting people across the country to round-the-clock banking services. He noted that nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts had been opened, enabling the direct transfer of government benefits to beneficiaries and helping eliminate leakages in the delivery of welfare assistance. The Prime Minister also highlighted the role of the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, PM SVANidhi and PM Vishwakarma in expanding access to formal credit. He said small entrepreneurs, street vendors, traditional artisans and workers in the unorganised sector were now able to access loans without the need for conventional collateral. According to PM Modi, around 13 crore people had become first-time entrepreneurs under the Mudra Yojana. He also highlighted financial assistance extended to Self-Help Groups representing 10 crore rural women. He credited the RBI, commercial banks and banking employees for expanding access to financial services, including through the widespread adoption of RuPay cards. Social Security Schemes Strengthen Financial Protection The Prime Minister also underlined the contribution of social security schemes in extending financial protection to vulnerable sections of society. He said the Atal Pension Yojana covered around nine crore citizens, including 38 lakh beneficiaries in Odisha. PM Modi highlighted the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, which provides accident insurance, and the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, which offers life insurance at affordable premiums. He said insurance coverage and timely claim payments had helped families cope with financial difficulties, describing these initiatives as an example of good governance. Cybersecurity Key to Protecting India’s Financial System Emphasising the importance of the newly inaugurated facilities, PM Modi said the focus of the past decade had been on bringing the unbanked into the formal banking system, while the coming decade would concentrate on making banking more efficient, reliable and secure. He warned that modern conflicts were no longer limited to conventional weapons, as cyberattacks could also target and weaken a country’s economy. PM Modi said protecting India’s expanding financial system from cybercriminals and cyberterrorists was essential as the country strengthened its economic position. He underscored the need for modern computing infrastructure, advanced cybersecurity capabilities and specialised training to address emerging threats. The new Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute are expected to strengthen the RBI’s technological infrastructure and cybersecurity preparedness. Odisha Emerging as a Growth Hub PM Modi also highlighted the growing economic potential of eastern India, describing the region as an important driver of the vision of Viksit Bharat. He said Odisha was expanding beyond its traditional mineral-based industries and developing new opportunities in semiconductors, electronics, data centres and advanced computing. The Prime Minister expressed confidence that the emerging sectors would create fresh opportunities for the state’s youth and contribute to Odisha’s economic transformation. He concluded by extending festive greetings and invoking the slogan “Jai Jagannath”. -PIB

national_raw_news.title: GeM Promotes 'The AABHAR Collection' to Showcase India's Cultural Heritage and Support ...
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Commerce & Industry GeM Promotes ‘The AABHAR Collection’ to Showcase India’s Cultural Heritage and Support Local Artisans AABHAR Collection Features 294 Product Listings from 10 State and Central Handloom and Handicraft Emporiums Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 2:42PM by PIB Delhi The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is promoting ‘The AABHAR Collection’, a dedicated digital storefront showcasing curated gift items and hampers that reflect India’s rich cultural heritage. The collection features products associated with the One District, One Product (ODOP) initiative and Geographical Indication (GI) tags, providing government buyers with convenient access to distinctive regional products while supporting artisans, weavers, rural entrepreneurs and women-led enterprises. The collection features 294 product catalogue listings from 10 State and Central Handloom and Handicraft Emporiums. These include COTTAGE from Central Cottage Industries Emporium, KHADI INDIA from the Khadi and Village Industries Commission, Garvi Gurjari (Gujarat), Himcrafts (Himachal Pradesh), Jharcraft (Jharkhand), Cauvery (Karnataka), Mrignayani (Madhya Pradesh), Marhati (Maharashtra), Purbashree (North East) and Poompuhar (Tamil Nadu). Seven additional government emporiums and organisations are at an advanced stage of completing the seller onboarding process, which will enable them to offer their curated products through the AABHAR Collection storefront. These include the Coffee Board, Manjusha and Biswa Bangla (West Bengal), Jammu & Kashmir Handloom & Handicrafts Marketing Corporation Ltd. (JKHHMC), Merakai (Nagaland), Utkalika (Odisha) and Panthoibi (Manipur). The proposed addition of their product catalogues is expected to further diversify the collection’s regional representation and product range. The collection includes handicrafts, handlooms, artisanal foods, pantry products and personal care items. It offers government buyers gifting options for official ceremonies, conferences, State events, foreign delegations, employee recognition, retirement functions and festive occasions. Speaking on the launch of the AABHAR Collection 2026 initiative, Chief Executive Officer, GeM, Shri Mihir Kumar, said, “The Aabhar Collection marks an important milestone in enhancing visibility of indigenous arts and crafts, showcasing the rich tapestry of Indian heritage and culture, and empowering underserved seller groups through the network of Central and State Handicraft and Handloom Emporiums.” Explaining the rationale behind the launch of ‘The AABHAR Collection’ in July 2024 and the current campaign, Additional Chief Executive Officer, GeM, and In-charge of Social Inclusion, Shri Ajit B. Chavan, said, “The idea was to provide an effective market linkage to the country’s artisanal ecosystem by integrating them through this #VocalForLocal storefront on GeM with the country’s public procurement landscape.” He added that the collection enables Ministries, Departments, public sector undertakings (PSUs) and other government buyers to meet their gifting requirements while supporting indigenous products and local livelihoods. Government buyers can explore the collection at https://gem.gov.in/Aabhar and contribute to promoting India’s cultural heritage and local enterprises through the procurement of #VocalForLocal gift hampers. *** C N Abhijith Narayanan/Shabbir Azad/Anushka Pandey (Release ID: 2328424) Visitor Counter : 446 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Assamese , Tamil , Telugu , Kannada Share -- words | -- min read Ministry of Commerce & Industry GeM Promotes ‘The AABHAR Collection’ to Showcase India’s Cultural Heritage and Support Local...

national_raw_news.title: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare observes Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 with ...
national_raw_news.content: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare observes Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 with Integrity Pledge Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare observes Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 with Integrity Pledge ANI | Updated: Oct 26, 2026 17:55 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 26 (ANI): Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) observed Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 with an Integrity Pledge-taking ceremony today at Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi, reaffirming its commitment to probity, transparency, accountability and ethical conduct in public administration. Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare, JP Nadda, administered the Integrity Pledge in the presence of Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare and AYUSH Ministry (Independent) Prataprao Jadhav and Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Anupriya Patel, to senior officers of the Ministry. Other officers and officials of the Ministry participated in the ceremony virtually from their respective offices, according to the release. Vigilance Awareness Week is observed annually during the week in which the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, falling on October 31, is commemorated. This year, the observance is being held from October 26 to November 1, 2026, on the theme "Probity for Prosperity". The theme underscores the significance of honesty, integrity and transparency as essential pillars of good governance and public trust in institutions. In keeping with the theme, the Vigilance Division of the Department of Health and Family Welfare is undertaking various activities under the Vigilance Awareness Campaign 2026 to strengthen vigilance awareness and promote ethical conduct among officers and staff of the Ministry and its subordinate offices, institutes and organisations. These initiatives seek to reinforce institutional accountability and foster a work environment guided by transparency, responsibility and adherence to established norms. The Integrity Pledge reaffirmed the commitment of officers and officials to uphold the rule of law, maintain the highest standards of probity and transparency in the discharge of their duties. It further emphasised the importance of acting in the public interest, demonstrating integrity through personal conduct, and reporting any instances of corruption to the appropriate authorities. The pledge underscored the collective responsibility of the Government, citizens and the private sector in combating corruption. It called for sustained vigilance and adherence to the highest standards of honesty and integrity in all spheres of public life. The observance reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to maintaining high standards of ethical conduct and accountability in the discharge of official responsibilities, in keeping with the principles of transparent, responsible and effective public administration.
